items.title: Consumer Discretionary - Travel and Vacation Providers Stocks Q2 Results: Benchmarking Norwegian Cruise Line (NYSE:NCLH)

items.title: Norwegian Cruise Line Just Dropped 16% in a Month: Sell Now, or Buy More?
items.summary: Norwegian Cruise Line shares shed a significant chunk of their value in a single month, but the culprit behind the selloff has nothing to do with the company itself, and that distinction changes the calculus entirely for investors deciding what to do next.

items.title: Oil Price Rally Helps Energy Stocks, Hurts Airlines
items.summary: The 5% jump in U.S. crude oil prices today is having some of the familiar effects we've seen in recent months across the market when tensions build in the Middle East.    Winners largely are coming from the energy sector, which is the best performing group in the S&P 500 today.

items.title: History Has An Opinion On This CCL Price Level
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL), the global cruise line operator, has pulled back about 14% from its early-August high near $29.67, settling near $25.37 a share after Wednesday's sector-wide selloff on rising fuel costs. That's a separate, steeper retreat from the stock's 52-week high of $34.03, set earlier this year.

items.title: Can NCLH's 2.5% Capacity CAGR Support a Free-Cash-Flow Inflection?
items.summary: Norwegian Cruise's slower fleet growth, nearly $1B annual capex reduction and $500M-plus savings could support a stronger free-cash-flow profile.
